subject: Predictions over new data with inla.posterior.sample/.eval()?

messages.author: eb9cf3e5f6c5cc0f
messages.subject: Predictions over new data with inla.posterior.sample/.eval()?
parts:
Hi,

I have fitted a model in INLA with some covariates as linear and some as RW1 (no spatial effect) and I am wondering if it is possible to predict over new data - get predicted y values from new values for the covariates (which I have) and this model fit. 

I have fit the model with the whole dataset, where this new data I have set the y observations to NA, but I am wondering if there is another way?   

Thanks in advance!
Erin

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Predictions over new data with inla.posterior.sample/.eval()?
parts:
Dear Erin,

You can use inla.posterior.sample() to sample the posterior distribution of the parameters. And combine those with your new data to get the predictions for the new data. Then you don't need to refit the model.

Best regards,

ir. Thierry Onkelinx

Thank you for your reply. I did try this but my predicted samples have very high probabilities (which doesn't really make sense with my data), so I was wondering if there was a way to do it similar to 'predict(fit, newdata)' where fit is the model fit without the NA values included and newdata is the dataframe of the covariate values associated with the NA values? 

(As an aside: when I run the model without the NA values the probabilities seem about right).  

Best wishes,
Erin

parts:
if you use to flexible models, like besag/rw1/rw2, then these works fine
just in the near future. if you're to far out, then the variance will
get high, hence the predictions are less useful
